title: MountainView pilot sync - units economics & throughput tuning
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on tokens/sec per dollar, observed caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Team reviewed last 48 hours of runs, looked at an unexpected tail latency spike, and agreed on tuning steps: increase prefix caching, test q8_0 quantization path, and run a 2-hour throughput benchmark at 75% traffic with smaller batch sizes. Action items include Redwood sending a tuned config and cost model spreadsheet; MountainView to provide additional representative prompt set and schedule infra window for benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-21 16:00 PST - Duration 42m - Attendees: Sofia R., Daniel C., Lena P. (Redwood) / Priya S., Ethan P., Rosa D., Markus L. (MountainView).

[00:00] Sofia: ok, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick run through the metrics from the pilot and then dig into tuning. i know there were some anomalies overnight.
[00:28] Priya: yeah hi, thanks, we saw tokens per dollar drop on one of the endpoints, curious if that's due to batching or a model fallback.
[00:45] Daniel: quick context, we rerouted a small percentage to the lower-tier fp16 variant late last night to avoid queueing, that can change unit cost and token throughput.
[01:10] Ethan: can you remind us the baseline numbers? we had been aiming for ~850 tokens / $ at 95%ile, right?
[01:25] Sofia: baseline was 820 tokens/$ averaged across the whole test set, but peak shapes were different. the last 24h average dropped to 560 tokens/$ on the search-summarize route because of longer generated outputs and fewer cache hits.
[01:50] Markus: also noticed a spike in tail latency around 02:00 our time, about 900ms p95 to p99 widening.
[02:05] Daniel: yeah that's likely KV cache misses plus a couple of big prompts with long context windows. we had continuous batching enabled, batch size target 32, but when the long prompt hits it forces a separate batch and serialization overhead increases.
[02:40] Rosa: so, batching helps cost but hurts latency on those edge cases?
[02:50] Daniel: exactly, it's the classic tradeoff. you get better tokens/sec/$ when batch fills, but if you have high variance length prompts you see tail spikes.
[03:10] Sofia: quick data point from the sheet we shared: enabling prefix caching on the top-20 prompts improved tokens/$ by ~28% in the last run window. that was with batch target 24.
[03:34] Priya: that 28% is great. what's the hit on accuracy we saw with the cached responses? any regression?
[03:45] Lena: we ran the smoke eval set and precision loss was minimal, about 0.6% delta in the top-5 rerank metric; worth it.
[04:02] Ethan: did you use TTL on the cache or sticky per-user? we need to be careful with stale outputs for product explanations.
[04:15] Daniel: TTL of 6 hours for now, and we keep a freshness flag. for high-sensitivity prompts (billing/account), we bypass cache.
[04:30] Priya: good. about quantization, we tried q8_0 on a small shard earlier, results?
[04:40] Daniel: q8_0 saved roughly 22% in inference compute and improved tokens/$ by 12% due to lower vram usage enabling higher concurrency, but in a few tests we saw slight logits jitter leading to minor hallucinations on corner cases.
[05:05] Markus: jitter is concerning; regulator-facing outputs need to be consistent. can we keep q8_0 for non-sensitive routes?
[05:15] Sofia: yes that's the plan, route policy can map sensitive routes to fp16/dedicated pool and bulk summarization to q8_0.
[05:25] Rosa: what about autoscaling? are we hitting any cold start issues when scale jumps?
[05:33] Daniel: we saw one cold start while scaling at 02:12, which matched the tail latency window. that was a scale-up to handle a burst, and the first 6 requests were routed to new containers without warm KV cache.
[05:50] Ethan: can we pre-warm the nodes for scheduled peaks? we have a nightly batch at 01:50 that often spikes.
[05:58] Daniel: yes, we can coordinate pre-warm windows and pin a small dedicated reserve during that hour. that would reduce misses.
[06:15] Priya: ok, tuning items summary so far: increase prefix caching set, test q8_0 on non-sensitive routes, schedule pre-warm for nightly spike, and reduce batch target for low-latency routes.
[06:35] Sofia: correct. also we recommend a micro-benchmark: 2-hour run at 75% traffic mix, target batch sizes 12 and 24, capture tokens/sec/$ and tail latencies.
[06:50] Priya: timeline? we need results before Friday because product team wants go/no-go for the next sprint.
[06:58] Lena: we can prepare tuned config by EOD Wednesday and run the benchmark Thursday morning, send results Thursday afternoon.
[07:10] Markus: one more ask — can we get a per-route cost breakdown? the sheet had combined numbers but we need route-level units.
[07:20] Sofia: yes, we'll break out per-route tokens/sec/$ and attach the annotated sheet.
[07:30] Ethan: about the cost model, are you including amortized dedicated reserve costs? we might commit to dedicated next quarter.
[07:40] Daniel: the current model assumes hosted on shared pool; we can produce a dedicated pricing scenario that shows amortized monthly reserve vs on-demand tokens cost.
[07:55] Priya: any mention of competitors in the eval? we were curious about Anthropic and the cloud incumbents.
[08:03] Sofia: we kept a short comparative column; Anthropic came close on coherence but cost per token was higher in our test for similar prompt mixes. cloud incumbents had better tooling for autoscaling but higher unit costs.
[08:25] Rosa: ok good. next steps and owners?
[08:30] Sofia: i'll summarize: Redwood sends tuned config + per-route cost sheet (Lena), Daniel runs q8_0 bench for non-sensitive routes and scripts pre-warm (Daniel), MountainView provides expanded prompt set and grants infra window (Priya + Markus), and both sides sync on Friday for go/no-go.
[08:55] Priya: sounds good. also, can we add an audit log sample for the caching decision? compliance wants to see TTL and bypass rules.
[09:05] Lena: yes we'll include an excerpt from the audit log and the RBAC mapping.
[09:12] Ethan: small nit, transcription shows some speaker overlaps in the recording — ignore minor attribution errors.
[09:20] Sofia: noted. any other questions?
[09:25] Rosa: none. thanks team.

Meeting end recap with explicit next steps included in the notes and sheet links: https://redwood.example.com/sheets/mv-pilot-econ-2026-08-21 and security docs link: https://redwood.example.com/security/mv-audit-excerpt-2026-08-21
